text:
Morgan Rivera: Heads-up — Acme Labs escalated. Their integration with /v1/embeddings started failing after a front-end change. Getting 400 / shape errors. Customer says it worked previously.

Samir Gupta: Can you paste the exact request body and the API response?

Morgan Rivera: Pasted repro from customer (redacted keys):
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"model\": \"text-embedding-3-small\",
  \"input\": [[\"Sign up for our beta\"]]
}
```
API response: 400 Bad Request
```json
{\"error\":{\"message\":\"invalid input shape: expected string or array of strings, got nested array\",\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\"}}
```

Morgan Rivera: They say the front-end code changed from sending a bare string to always wrapping in an array for internal consistency. Somehow it double-wrapped during serialization.

Alex Chen: This is a classic single-vs-batch double-wrap. Front-end probably does `JSON.stringify([value])` and then the fetch wrapper also wraps into an array. 

Jamie Patel: Also seeing reports of latency spikes from the same customer — they are sending huge 10k-item batches in one call and some also double-wrapped. Combined this causes backoffs/retries and throughput issues on their side.

Samir Gupta: Repro locally with curl (I ran this against sandbox):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{\"model\":\"text-embedding-3-small\",\"input\":[[\"hello world\"]]}'
echo\\n
```
Response: 400 with same message. If I send \"input\":\"hello world\" or \"input\":[\"hello world\"] it returns 200 with embeddings.

Alex Chen: Also we've had customers accidentally pass precomputed vectors (list of floats) into the embeddings endpoint. That returns a dimension mismatch in downstream steps or a validation error because embeddings endpoint expects text input, not numeric arrays. Example error I've seen: `422 Unprocessable Entity: expected string input but got numeric array`.

Morgan Rivera: Customer initially thought it was a dimension mismatch from model change. They compared our SDK return shape to their downstream similarity engine and blamed us. But the real cause was the client sending nested arrays; once unwrapped, dims match.

EmbedBot: Helpful hint: sending a single entry should be either a string or a single-element list. Avoid nesting. See docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/api/embeddings#input-format

Jamie Patel: Quick remediation steps for support to give customer:
- Check client serialization: make sure you don't both wrap and stringify. In JS, `body: JSON.stringify({model, input: texts})` where texts is either \"some text\" or `[\"a\",\"b\"]` but not `[[\"a\"]]`.
- For Python requests, avoid `json.dumps` twice. Use `requests.post(url, json={...})` not `data=json.dumps(...)` then `json.dumps` again.
- If you're sending precomputed vectors, use the `vector-import` API (internal) or the dedicated endpoint — embeddings endpoint expects text.
- Limit batch sizes to 64-256 items per request depending on model; very large batches increase latency and can trigger client retries.

Samir Gupta: Example JS fix we provided to the customer: 
```js
// BAD
const payload = { model: 'text-embedding-3-small', input: [texts] } // texts already an array
fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(payload) })
// if texts is itself an array-of-arrays you get nested arrays

// GOOD
const payload = { model: 'text-embedding-3-small', input: texts } // texts = [\"a\",\"b\"] or \"a\"
fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(payload) })
```

Alex Chen: Also suggested they add defensive validation client-side: ensure `Array.isArray(input)` and that typeof elements === 'string'. If element is array -> flatten or throw.

Morgan Rivera: Customer ran local fix, unwrapped inputs, switched to batches of ~128, and errors stopped. Latency improved and their retry storms went away. They reported an unexpected billing spike — appears to be due to aggressive retrying from their wrapper when it saw 400s; each retry generated new requests (we're following up whether failed requests were billed).

eng-oncall: FYI — I asked infra to check for any anomaly on our side during that window. No server-side rollout correlated. Looks client-only.

Jamie Patel: Follow-up actions:
- Support: send the JS + Python snippets and the single-line checklist we gave the customer.
- DevEx: add a short note in the quickstart about common double-wrap pitfalls and an FAQ entry.
- Eng-ML: consider clearer validation message when numeric arrays are passed (explicitly say \"received numeric vectors; did you mean vector-import endpoint?\").

Samir Gupta: I flagged this as P2, attaching repro. If anyone needs the exact customer payload I have the sanitized dump.

Morgan Rivera: Closing loop: customer confirmed fix in staging and scheduled a prod deploy. Marking support ticket RESOLVED from our side. :white_check_mark:

EmbedBot: Tip: when troubleshooting, ask for `curl -v` output and the raw JSON body. That usually reveals double-serialization quickly.
